newsitem.title: TANZANIA: 60 killed, thousands homeless in Tanzanian floods.
newsitem.headline: 60 killed, thousands homeless in Tanzanian floods.

text.p: Sixty people have died, many others are missing and thousands are homeless in southern Tanzania after widespread floods following torrential rains, a United Nations official said on Sunday.
"These people are living a nightmare," Irene Lacy, country director of the U.N. World Food Programme (WFP), said in a statement.
She said severe drought affected Tanzania for four months from last November and 670,000 people were in need of relief food.
"Then, after seeing an entire season's crop wither away, more than 50,000 of the same people in the Lindi region, southern Tanzania, were hit by torrential rains," she added.
Lacy said the floods had killed 60 people and made thousands homeless. Many were also missing.

WFP sent three plane-loads of food and shelter materials -- enough to feed 5,000 people for a week -- to the region. They are being distributed by helicopters and trucks to families stranded by floods.
In western Tanzania, five WFP trucks carrying food to camps for refugees from neighbouring Burundi were stranded for two days by flooded roads.
The WFP last week approved a major emergency operation to assist 200,000 people in drought-affected areas of Tanzania, involving the supply of 11,000 tonnes of food, Lacy said.
